source.title: Task 032 — Convert the digital-asset portfolio into an income-first execution backlog
source.body:
# Task 032 — Convert the digital-asset portfolio into an income-first execution backlog

**Parent programme:** Task 028 / portfolio roadmap — https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/issues/95  
**Related:** competitor/repository register https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/issues/114 · Stage 0 audit https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/issues/115 · customer evidence sprint https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/issues/116  
**Status:** Planning task registered; no revenue, customer validation, audit completion or deployment is implied.

## Objective

Bring every plausible digital asset and reusable capability into the portfolio's durable list of work to be done, while prioritising the shortest credible path to first income. The goal is not to build every idea. The goal is to identify what already exists, who may pay for it, what can be offered now as a service, and what minimum work is needed to deliver it reliably.

## Governing rule

**Sell a well-scoped service using existing skills/assets before investing in a new app.** Reuse/upgrade first; build only after evidence. Every item must have one canonical owner/repository, provenance and licence status, maturity evidence, buyer/customer, next action, dependencies/cost, risks, and a measurable validation or revenue milestone. Unknown means UNKNOWN, not assumed owned or ready.

## Full digital-asset families to inventory

1. **Portfolio, governance and operating systems:** personal portfolio/hub, repository and deployment registry, enterprise governance, reusable workflows, checklists, decision logs, task tracking and operating procedures.
2. **Software and PWAs:** existing apps, prototypes, modules, templates, APIs, integrations, offline workflows, dashboards, calculators, automation and mobile/web interfaces.
3. **Data and knowledge:** structured catalogues, farm/animal-health knowledge, supplier/buyer intelligence, public procurement information, competitor research, market evidence, taxonomies and reusable reference data (with source, licence, freshness and accuracy recorded).
4. **AI and automation:** AI Studio apps, prompts, agent workflows, model/API adapters, evaluation/test harnesses, local/offline fallbacks and free-tier API configuration guides. Never store API keys or secrets in Git.
5. **Content and intellectual property:** articles, research, guides, SOPs, templates, business plans, proposal/tender documents, training content, code, original designs, brand assets and downloadable products; verify authorship and commercial rights.
6. **Distribution and audience:** websites, domains, blogs, social profiles, newsletters, SEO assets, directories, opt-in lead channels, affiliate links, analytics and customer enquiry flows. Track account owner, consent, destination, performance and terms.
7. **Commercial infrastructure:** service packages, pricing hypotheses, quotation/proposal templates, contracts, supplier/customer onboarding, lead CRM, follow-up sequences, delivery checklists, case-study evidence and customer support.
8. **Relationships and market access:** permissioned supplier, buyer, farmer, integrator, SME, professional-provider, partner and funder relationships; track source, consent, last contact and next action without placing confidential personal data in public repositories.
9. **Research and funding assets:** grant/tender calendars, eligibility research, partner maps, application components, budgets and reporting templates. Verify current calls and eligibility before acting.
10. **Design and media:** original logos, visual systems, illustrations, photos, video/audio, product screenshots and presentation assets with licence/attribution and source files.
11. **Reusable technical foundations:** CI/build pipelines, test suites, security/privacy checklists, deployment recipes, backups, exports, documentation generators and common components.
12. **Legacy, duplicate and uncertain assets:** dormant apps, forks, templates, AI-generated scaffolds, experiments and near-duplicate projects. Classify reuse / upgrade / extract / archive / pause / rights-check; do not count forks or templates as wholly owned IP without evidence.
13. **Client/employer/third-party assets:** track separately as service relationships or authorised case studies only. WCD, MOSHA, YellowBlue, MegaDealsMA, Tshono and other third-party/client work are not automatically owned products; no changes or commercial reuse without permission.

## Income-first execution order

### P0 — Ten fixed-scope offers; sell before building (first 7 days)

**Pricing note:** The BWP amounts below are proposed test prices, not verified market rates or promises of income. Confirm scope, client ability to pay, delivery time, taxes/fees and competitor alternatives during discovery. Quote in writing; request a deposit where appropriate. Start by marketing the most relevant offers to each prospect, not by publishing all ten indiscriminately.

1. **Website & Digital Presence Health Check — test price BWP 750–1,500; 3–5 working days.** Review one website (up to 10 key pages), mobile usability, broken links, page titles/meta, contact details, basic accessibility signals, lead path and obvious technical risks. Deliver a prioritised findings report and 30-minute handover. Excludes penetration testing, guaranteed rankings, paid tools and implementing fixes.
2. **Website Care & Monthly Change Plan — test price BWP 500–1,200/month for a defined small site.** Monthly uptime/basic availability checks, one scheduled content change, link/contact-form spot check and short status report. Define hosting access, response windows, backup responsibilities and exclusions first. Hosting fees, emergency recovery, redesign and third-party subscriptions are extra.
3. **One-Page Lead-Generating Website / Landing Page — test price BWP 1,500–3,500.** One responsive page using client-approved copy/assets, one clear offer, contact/WhatsApp CTA, basic metadata and handover instructions. Client supplies approved branding, domain/hosting access and factual claims. Excludes e-commerce, custom backend, paid integrations and ongoing hosting.
4. **Local Search & Business Profile Improvement Pack — test price BWP 900–2,000.** Audit and improve one eligible business's local-search information, service descriptions, on-page local signals and review-response guidance. Profile changes are subject to platform verification/eligibility; no guaranteed ranking, reviews or lead volume.
5. **WhatsApp Enquiry & Lead-Tracking Setup — test price BWP 750–1,800.** Configure a simple enquiry path with approved click-to-chat links, intake questions, a lightweight lead tracker and follow-up templates. No bulk unsolicited messaging, unofficial API automation or transfer of customer data into public repositories.
6. **SME Workflow & AI Opportunity Assessment — test price BWP 750–1,500.** One 60–90-minute discovery session for one workflow, followed by a process map, bottlenecks, free/low-cost tool options, risk/privacy notes and a prioritised implementation plan. No claim that AI is necessary; no implementation included.
7. **Small Workflow Automation Implementation — test price BWP 1,500–5,000 after scoping.** Implement one bounded, low-risk workflow using client-approved tools, with test cases, handover notes and rollback steps. API/subscription costs, regulated decisions, high-risk data processing and ongoing support are excluded unless separately approved.
8. **Tender & Supplier Readiness Check — test price BWP 750–2,000.** Review one opportunity or supplier-readiness checklist against the published requirements; produce a gap list, document checklist and action plan. Client retains responsibility for truth and submission. Excludes legal advice, certification, paid registrations and any promise of eligibility, award or funding.
9. **Supplier / Product Sourcing Shortlist — test price BWP 1,000–3,000 for a defined category and shortlist.** Research a specified product/category and provide a small evidence-based shortlist with public contact/source links, comparison criteria and verification questions. No guarantee of supplier legitimacy, stock, price, import clearance or delivery; samples, freight, duties and due diligence are separate.
10. **Business Operations & Digital Asset Audit — test price BWP 1,000–2,500.** Review one small business's supplied public-facing digital assets and one agreed workflow; deliver an asset/ownership register, risks, quick wins and 30-day action plan. Excludes legal/IP opinions, financial audit, security penetration testing and access to systems not expressly authorised.

- [ ] Create a one-page offer sheet for each offer, stating buyer/problem, deliverables, exclusions, client inputs, turnaround, test price, payment terms, acceptance criteria and next step.
- [ ] Rank offers for immediate outreach by existing capability, low delivery cost, urgency of buyer problem, ability to show evidence and ease of reaching decision-makers. Do not imply all ten are ready to deliver until the required assets and QA are checked.
- [ ] Inspect the existing portfolio enquiry/WhatsApp funnel (including Task 067) and ensure each offer has a clear call to action, structured intake, consent, source attribution and manual follow-up path.
- [ ] Build a small, permission-safe prospect list from public business information; record why each prospect is relevant. No mass spam, scraping against terms, or fabricated personalisation.
- [ ] Contact a small, relevant batch of prospects personally; track replies, meetings, objections, quoted price and paid-pilot decisions. Do not claim a lead or sale until confirmed.
- [ ] After the first buyer conversations, revise or remove prices that are not supported by customer response and measured delivery effort.

### P1 — Audit assets that can support the first offers (days 1–14)

- [ ] MOKORO Digital Growth Engine + FAROUKPANDORCONSULTANT: map current working features, service fit, deployment and delivery gaps.
- [ ] Local QA Reviewer / website-care tools: inspect existing repo/prototype; demonstrate only verified checks and clearly label manual vs automated coverage.
- [ ] Tender & Supplier Readiness: reuse verified public sources and create a human-reviewed readiness service before building a monitoring product.
- [ ] MOKORO Enterprise OS: reuse governance/templates as internal delivery infrastructure; do not turn it into a catch-all client app.
- [ ] Check existing AI Studio prototypes and domain/blog assets for useful, owned components; record exportability, licence, account ownership and recurring costs.
- [ ] Use the existing AgriSage360 broiler calculator as a candidate for a small, explicitly scoped farm-planning service only after current PR checks, usability and content review. It is not evidence of customer demand or revenue.

### P2 — Validate the next commercial products (days 7–30)

- [ ] Interview target buyers for website care/QA, tender-supplier readiness and clothing/embroidery production workflows.
- [ ] Select only one next product based on evidence of a painful problem, buyer authority, willingness to pay, access to customers, delivery effort, support burden and risk.
- [ ] Prototype with synthetic/sample data; seek a paid pilot or a specific written commitment before expanding features.
- [ ] Assess the existing clothing/embroidery workflow only with proper employer/client permission and without exposing confidential production/customer records.
- [ ] Maintain impact-funded and regulated concepts in a separate track; do not rely on uncertain grants as near-term household income.

### P3 — Portfolio-wide inventory and consolidation

- [ ] For each plausible asset, record canonical name/ID, repository or account URL, owner/rights/provenance, asset class, current status, evidence checked/date, customer/problem, revenue/funding hypothesis, next action, dependencies/cost, risk, reuse decision and review date.
- [ ] Map all listed repositories, deployments, AI Studio apps, domains, blogs, content, datasets, code libraries, affiliate assets and service templates to the inventory.
- [ ] Resolve duplicate families (farm/animal health; directories/property/commerce; AI orchestration; QA/security; learning/skills; ERP/OS) only after inspecting source and actual deployments.
- [ ] Distinguish original code, fork, template, generated scaffold, client work and uncertain rights.
- [ ] Create a ranked income-readiness view: **sellable service now / requires small fix / requires buyer validation / partner or regulation dependent / long-term experiment / archive or rights-check**.
- [ ] Keep the inventory in one canonical register in the portfolio repository; detailed implementation stays in the relevant repo and links back to the canonical item.

## Minimum register fields

Asset ID; canonical name; asset family; canonical repo/account/domain; enterprise; owner and rights evidence; provenance/licence; current status; last verified date; actual tests/deployment evidence; dependencies and operating cost; customer/problem; existing alternative/competitor; offer or monetisation hypothesis; first buyer/partner; next action; estimated effort; risks/approvals; reuse decision; measurable success criterion; revenue evidence (none until verified); linked issues/PRs.

## Weekly operating scorecard

Report counts for assets inventoried and rights-checked; offers published; relevant prospects contacted; replies; discovery calls; proposals; paid pilots; cash collected; delivery hours; direct costs; gross margin; repeat/renewal signals; blockers and stop decisions. Use actual values only. Review weekly and conduct monthly managing-director sign-off.

## Stop rules

- No new repository solely because a name or idea exists.
- No paid API, SaaS, advertising, domain or infrastructure spend without explicit approval and a justified budget.
- No unverified deployment, customer, revenue, grant, certification or competitor-superiority claims.
- No client/employer repository edits or reuse of their data/IP without explicit authorisation.
- If a workstream has no buyer evidence, feasible delivery path or justified funding partner, pause it rather than letting it displace income-generating work.

## First acceptance gate

The first completion report must show: (1) all ten fixed-scope offer sheets with delivery boundaries and clearly marked test prices; (2) the existing lead funnel and gaps; (3) a shortlist of 20–30 relevant prospects or channels grounded in public evidence; (4) a dated audit of the assets directly needed to deliver those offers; and (5) actual outreach/response results or an explicit blocker. It must not substitute more app ideas for customer contact.

**Immediate next action:** prepare the ten offer sheets, inspect the enquiry funnel, select the best-fit initial offers for prospect conversations, and start outreach while Task 030/031 audits continue. Inventory breadth is important, but near-term income depends on offers, buyer conversations, delivery and payment—not the number of repositories.

## Execution update — 2026-10-19

### Completed
- Added `docs/INCOME-FIRST-OFFER-CARDS.md` to the portfolio control repository.
- Commit: `27a0d37b61acbb76a35fbaea6d1c3d82a6f8e11a`
- File: https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/blob/main/docs/INCOME-FIRST-OFFER-CARDS.md
- Contains 10 bounded service-offer drafts, proposed test-price ranges clearly labelled as unvalidated, scope/exclusions, acceptance criteria, readiness gates, and stop rules.
- Recommended first tests: website/digital-presence health check, business operations/digital asset audit, and SME workflow assessment.

### Evidence reviewed
- MOKORO Digital Growth Engine README and client-acquisition tool source: local-first workflow; deployment must be verified before promising hosted availability.
- FAROUKPANDORCONSULTANT README: business administration/secretarial service-line positioning and regulated-service boundaries.
- Existing Task 030 / issue #115 and Stage 0 audit notes.

### Important risks preserved
- YellowBlue is explicitly client/third-party work. Its September audit documents a serious form-submission regression (fake success tickets; no backend), customer PII in reachable Git history, and credentials previously shared over WhatsApp. Do not modify the client repo or purge history without the client's explicit authorization. Any client communication should accurately disclose the form limitation.
- AgriSage outstanding register reports 39 open and 26 in-progress items, with key legal, privacy, Firestore-rules, source-verification and market-readiness gaps. Do not position it as a production veterinary/legal/financial service based on README claims.
- The Firebase web API key issue requires restriction/rules verification, not blind rotation; prior scans are documented but were not independently rerun in this execution pass.

### Not yet done
- No outreach was sent; no prospect contacted; no prices or demand validated.
- No builds/tests or live deployments were run.
- No client-owned repo, secret, DNS setting or production deployment was changed.
- Next: inspect and test the existing offer-delivery assets and enquiry funnel, then run a small, permission-safe prospect validation sprint.

## Execution update — 2026-10-19 (delivery and validation assets)

### Added and verified in the portfolio repository
1. [Website health-check delivery checklist](https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/blob/main/docs/WEBSITE-HEALTH-CHECK-DELIVERY-CHECKLIST.md)  
   Commit: `ade5ea64fb629a8bb49313ade68176206b7aa22`  
   Includes scope/permission gate, evidence standards, finding severity/confidence, test categories, report structure, and quality gate. It explicitly does not claim a sample audit was performed.
2. [First customer validation shortlist](https://github.com/faroukpandor/faroukpandor.github.io/blob/main/docs/FIRST-CUSTOMER-VALIDATION-SHORTLIST-2026-10-19.md)  
   Commit: `8a541ed098481878e4c7b660d4e04ccd36ec7ab3`  
   Contains seven direct prospect hypotheses and referral channels, sourced from public pages, with qualification questions, a draft outreach note and an actual-results scorecard. It explicitly records zero outreach sent.

### Technical verification findings
- MOKORO package scripts include `test:deploy`, `verify:static`, `verify:live`, and focused test scripts.
- The repository HANDOFF.md records prior test results from 2026-10-09 (TypeScript clean; Learn 195, Cloud 323, Intake 23, Deploy 65, Compare 105 passing). These are historical project notes, not a fresh run in this execution.
- Current live host checks could not be completed through the available web inspection path. No local install/build/test or live verification was run. Therefore current deployment, tests and form delivery remain unverified.

### Next gate
Run the existing verification scripts in an authorised environment with dependencies installed, then test one chosen prospect's public customer journey without submitting forms or changing accounts. Contact only after current fit and contact route are verified; no message has been sent.

## Verified technical blocker — 2026-10-19

Read-only inspection of MOKORO GitHub Actions found the latest visible `MOKORO Quality Gates` run for PR #43 failed on 2026-10-18: https://github.com/faroukpandor/MOKORO---Digital-Growth-Engine/actions/runs/39098460134

Evidence from job `Specification, safety, tests and builds`:
- Specification coverage passed.
- Deployment configuration check passed.
- `scripts/test-cloud.mjs` failed its drift check: `the generated Cloudflare copies are current — got: ""`.
- The shared Cloudflare/server logic suite reports **322 passed, 1 failed**; the failing assertion is the generated `functions/_lib/*.js` copies matching their `src/lib/*.ts` sources.
- Later intake, learning-content, competitive-claims, marketing-hygiene and build steps were skipped after the failure. Do not treat the run as a successful release check.

Next safe action: on an authorized checkout of the exact PR head, run `npm ci`, `npm run build:functions`, then `npm run test:cloud`, review the generated diff, and rerun the full quality-gates workflow. Do not amend or merge PR #43 automatically; it is a separate research PR and requires its own review. No deployment, external outreach, or client-repository change was made as part of this inspection.
